(b) Every OBSERVED caller of `applyRigDeform`/`rigResetPose`/`rigCommitFrame`/`rigDragIKEnd` calls `SMEngineBridge.renderNow()` itself, immediately after, on the OUTSIDE of the call — confirmed for all seven external call sites (rig-bridge.js:433/454/483/566, timeline.js:11568-inside-rigCommitFrame-itself/11576) — and `renderNow`'s own non-viewportOnly branch (engine-bridge.js:4275-4326, cited by line only) ALWAYS calls `buildSceneJson()` fresh rather than being gated on `window._sceneVersion` (its own comment at :4301 states plainly: 'scene may have mutated without a version bump (eraser/select drags) — never let a stale drag-cache survive this'), so the freshly-mutated live geometry is picked up on the very next render regardless of whether `_smGeomDirty` fired.

`rigCommitFrame`'s own undo hook: `if(!ld._rigPoseUndoPushed)pushUndo();ld._rigPoseUndoPushed=false;` (2546-2547) — pushes ITS OWN undo checkpoint only when no drag-start checkpoint already exists (the flag rig-bridge.js sets to `true` at 317-318), then UNCONDITIONALLY resets the flag to `false` regardless of which branch ran, so the NEXT commit (with no intervening drag) always gets its own fresh checkpoint. This exact skip-if-already-pushed rationale is documented in BOTH files identically (app.js:2540-2545 and rig-bridge.js:296-299, cited by line only): a checkpoint taken AFTER a drag has already live-mutated `bone.segments` would pair an already-posed rig with the frame's still-unbaked (pre-commit) strokes, an internally inconsistent undo snapshot.

What `rigCommitFrame` writes into which frame store, and the load-bearing ORDER: `ensureKeyframe()` (2548, tools.js:1882, cited by name only) runs FIRST — it captures `getEffectiveStrokes()` for the CURRENT (pre-repose) frame content into a fresh keyframe's `strokes`, then calls `loadFrame()` internally, which REBUILDS the layer's live Paper items from that just-baked (still undeformed-by-THIS-commit) data, discarding the in-progress posed geometry on screen and invalidating the OLD `b._live`/`b._liveRaster` references. `relinkRigBinds(ld,userLayers[state.activeLayerIdx])` (2549, C21h, cited by name only) then re-resolves fresh `_live`/`_liveRaster` pointers onto the items `loadFrame` just created. `applyRigDeform(ld)` (2550, THIS scope's own packet 1) is called a SECOND time, re-applying the SAME pose (still sitting untouched in `rig.bones[...].segments`, since neither `ensureKeyframe` nor `loadFrame` touch `ld.rig`) onto these fresh Paper items. ONLY THEN is `ld._rigPoseLive=false` set (2551) and `saveActiveLayerFrame()` called (2552) — the ordering here is load-bearing for a SEPARATE reason: `saveActiveLayerFrame` (app.js:4634, cited by line only) has its OWN early-return guard at app.js:4663 that includes `||ld._rigPoseLive||` — had `_rigPoseLive` still been `true` at this point, the save would silently no-op and the freshly re-deformed geometry would never reach `ld.frames[i].strokes`. `saveActiveLayerFrame` itself serializes the NOW live-deformed Paper children back into the frame's stored `strokes` array (via its own `serP`-based path, C21d lineage, cited by name only) — so the persisted write is INDIRECT (through the live Paper layer), not a direct `ld.frames[i].strokes=...` assignment inside this scope's own lines.

Whether `rigCommitFrame` clears the pose afterward: NO. It does not reset `rig.bones[...].segments` to rest (that is exclusively `rigResetPose`'s own job, packet 2, a DIFFERENT user action). `ld._rigPoseLive=false` (2551) is a UI/autosave-guard STATE flag ('the drag is no longer in-progress/uncommitted'), not a geometry reset — the bones remain in their posed positions after Commit, matching the header comment's own framing ('bakes the current LIVE pose into a keyframe'): the posed shape becomes the new frame's baked content, and a subsequent `rigResetPose` call would be needed to return the rig to rest.

The IK maths, packets 4-5: `rigSetIK(ld,rootRef,jointRef,endRef,flip)` (2561) resolves each of `rootRef`/`jointRef`/`endRef` — each shaped `{boneId,vi}` (confirmed by `rigAnchorPoint`'s own destructuring at 2570-2571 and by rig-bridge.js's own `findIKChain`, out of scope, cited by name only, which constructs these refs) — to a world point via `rigAnchorPoint(rig,ref)` (2569-2573, THIS scope's own packet 4: reads `bone.segments[ref.vi]`, falling back to `bone.restSegments[ref.vi]` if the bone has never been posed, and returns `null` if the bone or that vertex index doesn't exist). It computes the two REST bone-segment lengths `l1`/`l2` (2565, `Math.hypot`) from the CURRENT positions of root/joint/end at the moment `rigSetIK` is called (i.e., whatever pose the rig happens to be in when the chain is first set — this is the chain's fixed 'rigidity' length from then on, not re-derived from `restSegments`), and writes a NEW entry into `rig.ikChains` keyed `boneId+':'+vi` of the END ref (2566), storing `{root,joint,end,l1,l2,flip:!!flip}` — `rigSetIK` never mutates any bone's `segments`/`restSegments` itself, only registers the chain. `rigDragIKEnd(ld,endKey,x,y)` (2574, packet 5) looks up the chain by `endKey` (2575), computes the world delta from the ROOT bone's CURRENT position to the drag target `(x,y)` (2577), clamps the reachable distance to `[|l1-l2|, l1+l2]` (2579-2580, the law-of-cosines chain's own reach limits, epsilon-padded to avoid a degenerate acos domain error at the exact extremes), solves the joint angle via the law of cosines with the `flip` sign choosing which of the two valid elbow solutions (2582-2584), WRITES the joint bone's own vertex point (2585) and the end bone's own vertex point (2596, reconstructed from the SAME clamped distance/angle rather than the raw drag target — 2588-2594's own comment explains why: using the raw unclamped target would silently stretch the joint-end segment past `l2` whenever the drag target was unreachable), then calls `applyRigDeform(ld)` (2597, this scope's own packet 1) to re-deform the bound strokes/meshes from the newly-solved bone positions before returning `true`. `rigDragIKEnd` does NOT touch the coincident 'near end of the END bone' companion vertex some chains have (rig-bridge.js's own `_posing.ld.rig.bones[chain.endNear...]` copy, rig-bridge.js:441-442, cited by line only, done by the CALLER immediately after) — see `future_proposals`.

Render-path vs gesture-path: NONE of this scope's six symbols is ever called from `getEffectiveStrokes` (app.js:2949, cited by line only) or from `buildSceneJson`/`scenePayload` (engine-bridge.js, cited by name only) — confirmed by a whole-src grep restricted to engine-bridge.js/tools.js/motion.js/select-bridge.js/tweens.js/export.js returning zero hits for any of the six symbol names. This is the entire reason the live-mutation-without-`_sceneVersion`-bump pattern above is safe in practice: every gesture path that mutates geometry also explicitly calls `SMEngineBridge.renderNow()` itself afterward (see prior finding), so no automatic/passive render path is ever expected to observe this scope's writes without an explicit render request alongside it.

packets.responsibility: Lead-in (2290-2292, 3 comment lines): states the live-preview-before-commit contract — called on every pose drag tick AND once more right before rigCommitFrame's own bake, so the committed keyframe always matches exactly what was last seen live. `applyRigDeform(ld)` (2293-2518): the SOLE deformer.
